cards.signin: {{cast.user}} signs in to {{cast.company}} inside the app itself; PingOne checks the password, the app never sends it anywhere else.
cards.pkce: Even if someone catches the code meant for {{cast.agent}}, it is useless without the secret {{cast.agent}} kept back.
cards.par: {{cast.agent}} hands its whole request to PingOne first, so nothing in it can be changed on the way through the browser.
cards.jar: {{cast.agent}} signs its request to {{cast.company}}, so PingOne can tell that nobody edited the scope or the redirect on the way.
cards.clientCredentials: At {{cast.company}}, the {{cast.serviceWord}} gets a token for itself, with no {{cast.userWord}} in the picture.
cards.lifecycle: {{cast.agent}} keeps {{cast.user}}'s session alive with a refresh token, until {{cast.company}} revokes it and the next refresh is refused.
cards.userinfo: {{cast.agent}} reads who {{cast.user}} is from PingOne, with {{cast.user}}'s own access token.
cards.device: {{cast.user}} links the {{cast.company}} TV app by typing a short code on the phone; the TV never sees the password.
cards.ciba: {{cast.agent}} needs {{cast.user}}'s go-ahead while {{cast.user}} is away from the app: PingOne asks on {{cast.user}}'s own device and {{cast.agent}} waits.
cards.tokenExchange: {{cast.user}}'s token is exchanged for one {{cast.agent}} can use, and the new token still says who acted for whom.
cards.piflow: {{cast.company}}'s own app renders the sign-in: PingOne answers with JSON instead of a login page.
